name: Hamstring stretch
pattern: Static hold: the hip bends with the knee straight, lengthening the back of the thigh.
setup: Lie on your back, loop a strap or towel around one foot.
Other leg flat on the floor or bent with the foot down.
Low back relaxed on the floor, not flattened hard.

steps.text: Raise the leg with the knee straight until you feel a pull behind the thigh.
Stay still 15-30 s. Keep the knee straight and the hips level on the floor.
Come out slowly, then switch sides.

cues.cue: Tip from the hips, back long. Lead with your belly button, not your head.
cues.why: Stretching with the pelvis tipped forward gained more hamstring length than with a rounded back.

cues.cue: Knee straight but not locked hard.
cues.why: A bent knee takes the stretch off the hamstrings.

cues.cue: Ease in to a mild pull, never pain.
cues.why: Gentle stretches still gain range; stretching into pain did not help and can irritate the muscle.

cues.cue: Hold 15-30 s, 2-4 times, about 60 s in total per side.
cues.why: 30 s holds gave the same gains as 60 s; aim for at least 5 min per muscle each week, most days.

cues.cue: Best after training. Before, keep it under 60 s per muscle and finish with a dynamic warm-up.
cues.why: Short holds cost almost no strength or power; long holds (60 s or more) do. Stretching does not speed recovery.

breathing: Breathe slowly and normally. Ease a little deeper as you breathe out.

tempo.note: Ease in for about 3 s, hold 15-30 s, ease out. Repeat 2-4 times each side.

mistakes.name: Rounding the back
mistakes.looks: You reach for your toes by curling the spine; the pelvis stays tucked.
mistakes.fix: Chest up, back long, fold from the hips. Bend less, feel more.
mistakes.why: The low back takes the stretch instead of the hamstrings.

mistakes.name: Knee bends
mistakes.looks: The knee drifts bent to reach further.
mistakes.fix: Straighten the knee and accept less range.
mistakes.why: It shortens the hamstrings and removes the stretch.

mistakes.name: Bouncing
mistakes.looks: You bob in and out of the stretch instead of holding still.
mistakes.fix: Ease in slowly, then stay still and let it relax.
mistakes.why: Bouncing triggers the muscle to tighten back and can strain it.

mistakes.name: Holding your breath
mistakes.looks: You tense up: shoulders creep up, jaw tight, breath held.
mistakes.fix: Breathe slowly; let each breath out take you a little deeper.
mistakes.why: Tension fights the stretch; relaxed breathing lets the muscle let go.

safety: Sharp, burning or tingling pain down the leg is a nerve, not a muscle: ease off.
Recent hamstring tear: wait for pain-free walking and go gently.
Back pain: use the lying version, not standing toe touches.

variants.change: Strap around the foot: lets you keep the back flat and the knee straight.
Toes pulled up: adds the calf and nerve tension; feels stronger, hold a little less deep.
Contract-relax: push gently against the stretch for 3-6 s, relax, then ease deeper. Similar range gains to static holds; also best after training.
A partner moves the limb. Go slowly and say when you feel a mild pull; the partner holds there, never pushes into pain.
Moving version: controlled swings through the range, 8-12 reps. Better before training than long holds.

easier: seated on a chair, leg out

subtypes.name: Lying hamstring stretch
subtypes.change: On your back, one leg up with a strap, hands or a wall. Safest for the back.

subtypes.name: Raised-leg hamstring stretch
subtypes.match: leg up|high leg|raised leg|on box|leg extended|on exercise ball
subtypes.change: Standing, heel on a low step or bench, leg straight; hinge forward with a flat back.

subtypes.name: Seated hamstring stretch
subtypes.change: Sit tall, one leg straight in front; lean forward from the hips.

subtypes.name: Half-kneeling hamstring stretch
subtypes.change: One knee down, front leg straight with the heel on the floor; sit the hips back.

subtypes.name: Wide-leg forward fold
subtypes.change: Feet wide, hinge forward with a long back, hands toward the floor. Inner thighs join in.

subtypes.name: Standing forward fold
subtypes.match: toe touch|toe touching|forward bend|fold|reach down|front hamstring|standing|toe (up|down)|bend
subtypes.change: Standing, knees soft, hinge forward and let the arms hang toward your feet.

metrics.label: Movement during hold
metrics.good: < 3° once you are in the stretch

motion.basis: Hold time and dose from garber2011, bandy1994, thomas2018; pelvic position from sullivan1992. Joint angles are estimates for an average adult (straight-leg raise about 70-80° in healthy adults is common clinical knowledge, not measured here).
